title: 12th Sitting of second session of 2026

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/12/2/2026).

Question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to the Minister of Health, Family and Welfare Aqeela Ali: many Maldivians are sent abroad for treatment at great cost to the state, which would fall if those services were available at home; what is the government's long-term plan to reduce reliance on overseas healthcare, how will it be implemented, and when will practical work begin?

Question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to the Minister of Health, Family and Welfare Aqeela Ali: there is no legal barrier to performing post-mortems in the Maldives, yet the state pays to send them abroad each time; why is this not done locally, does the government intend to start, and from what date?

First reading of the resolution submitted by Kendhoo MP Mauroof Zakir noting that, under the name of reducing staff at state-owned companies, many people are being dismissed from their jobs for political reasons, and seeking the views of Parliament's members on the matter.
Continuation of the debate on the bill to amend the Waste Management Act (Law No. 24/2022), submitted on behalf of the government by Ungoofaaru MP Ibrahim Shifaz.

Report of the State-Owned Enterprises Committee on the President's request for Parliament's consent to a member appointed to the Privatization and Corporatization Board, under Article 4(a) and (b) of the Privatization, Corporatization, Monitoring and Evaluation of State Businesses Act (Law No. 3/2013).
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: The sitting questioned the health minister on overseas treatment and post-mortems, gave a first reading to a resolution on political dismissals at state companies, continued the Waste Management Act amendment debate, and took a committee report on a Privatization Board appointment.
